Operator: Good day, and welcome to the VeriStream Communications Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to VeriStream Communications' Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Mark Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Network Officer; and other members of our leadership team. Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Mark Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for Q3. We exceeded expectations in several key areas. First, we saw robust net subscriber additions across residential and business segments, underscoring our broadband-first momentum. Second, our content and media operations delivered impressive revenue growth and profitability alongside strong subscriber gains. Third, our new product launches like 5G Ultra Home and StreamFusion are driving meaningful revenue and growth. Fourth, our revenue mix is evolving favorably with higher contributions from high-margin areas. Finally, we are strategically positioning ourselves through disciplined operating expense management that bolsters profitability. We are seeing very positive results from our investments in 5G convergence and fiber expansions, and their impact on customer retention and ARPU is significant. These efforts affirm our fiber-plus-5G strategy in a landscape shaped by fiber overbuilders, wireless alternatives, and streaming shifts.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Mark. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $32.5 billion, up 5% year-over-year. Our adjusted EBITDA was $10.2 billion, resulting in a margin of 31.4%. We are maintaining strict cost discipline. Capital expenditures were $4.5 billion, primarily allocated to 5G rollout and fiber expansion.

Before diving deeper into the P&L, I'd like to highlight our strong subscriber momentum, which continues to underpin our broadband-first strategy amid a competitive landscape dominated by fiber overbuilders like AT&T Fiber and Verizon Fios, as well as wireless disruptors such as T-Mobile's 5G Home Internet and emerging satellite players like Starlink. Let's start with net subscriber additions by segment, reported in revenue-generating units or RGUs. In Q3, we delivered total broadband and mobility net adds of 285,000 RGUs, exceeding our guidance midpoint by 15% and marking our 11th straight quarter of positive postpaid net adds. This represents a 12% year-over-year increase from 255,000 in Q3 2022, driven by disciplined pricing, enhanced bundling, and accelerated network investments. Churn remained best-in-class at 1.1% for residential broadband—below the industry average of 1.4% per New Street Research benchmarks—and 0.8% for business services.

In the residential segment, we added a robust 235,000 net RGUs, up 14% year-over-year and accelerating from 210,000 in Q2. This was fueled by our residential broadband RGU growth of 180,000 net adds—our strongest quarter since Q4 2021—primarily from fiber-to-the-home expansions and hybrid fiber-coax upgrades to DOCSIS 4.0, now covering 65% of our 25 million-home footprint. Gigabit-plus speeds drove 42% of these adds, with average residential broadband ARPU climbing 3.2% year-over-year to $68, thanks to our 'Gigabit Guarantee' promotion and selective 5-7% price increases on 10-year legacy customers, which saw voluntary churn under 0.5%.

Video RGUs contributed 35,000 net adds, reversing two quarters of modest declines, as our Xfinity Stream-like skinny bundle—now rebranded as VeriStream Flex with Peacock and Netflix integrations—retained 85% of at-risk households amid cord-cutting pressures. Mobile postpaid net adds hit 20,000, a 25% quarter-over-quarter ramp-up from Spectrum Mobile's playbook, with our MVNO on Verizon's network hitting 8.5 million lines and penetration rising to 28% of broadband homes. Regionally, the Northeast and Sun Belt markets led with 60% of adds—Northeast up 22% year-over-year on FTTH overbuild wins against Verizon, capturing 15% share in key MSAs like Boston and Philly, while the Sun Belt benefited from population in-migration and 5G fixed wireless access trials serving 50,000 unbundled homes as a cable alternative.

Strategically, we're leaning into 'quad-play' bundling, where 62% of new residential adds took three-plus services, boosting blended ARPU by 5% and lowering churn by 20 basis points. Looking ahead, we expect residential net adds of 220,000-250,000 in Q4, supported by $1.2 billion in capex for 2.5 million new FTTH passes, targeting underserved suburban pockets where cable penetration lags fiber at 40% versus 55% nationally per FCC data.

Shifting to the business segment, we achieved 50,000 net RGUs, a standout 22% year-over-year increase from 41,000, outpacing the segment's historical 5-10% growth amid enterprise spending normalization post-COVID. Small-and-medium business drove 32,000 net adds—up 18% year-over-year—with hosted voice and SD-WAN solutions gaining traction; our 'VeriStream Edge' platform, akin to Comcast Business's offerings, now serves 1.2 million SMB locations, with multi-gig symmetric speeds up to 10G converting 28% of trials to contracts.

Enterprise net adds of 18,000 RGUs were propelled by high-margin fiber lit buildings—now 45% of our 150,000-building portfolio—and private 5G networks, where we secured three major deals with logistics firms mirroring FedEx's playbook, totaling 5,000 RGUs for edge computing and IoT backhaul. ARPU here surged 7% year-over-year to $1,250 per seat, reflecting premium services like low-latency 5G slicing for AR/VR applications and dark fiber leases amid hyperscaler demand, such as AWS Direct Connect integrations.

Regionally, business strength was concentrated in the Midwest and West Coast, with 55% of adds; Midwest enterprise grew 30% on manufacturing reshoring, for example winning 2,000 RGUs from auto suppliers in Michigan, while California saw SMB acceleration from remote-hybrid work trends, offsetting competitive pressure from Lumen's enterprise divestitures. Churn ticked up slightly to 0.9% due to one-off contract expirations but remains below peers like Lumen at 1.5%.

Overall, these subscriber dynamics validate our 'Fiber + 5G Convergence' thesis, positioning us to capture 15-20% market share in a $200 billion addressable U.S. broadband/services market growing at 4% CAGR per Dell'Oro Group. With broadband now 72% of total RGUs and business comprising 25% of revenue, up from 22% year-over-year, we're on track for 400,000-450,000 full-year net adds, funding mid-single-digit EBITDA growth.

Now, let's turn to our content and media segment performance, which continues to be a high-growth engine amid the streaming wars and cord-cutting acceleration. This segment, encompassing our flagship SVOD platform StreamGlobal, linear cable networks like GlobalSportsNet and FamilyMax, and emerging FAST channels via FreeStream, delivered robust results driven by subscriber momentum, ARPU expansion, and targeted content investments.

Content and media revenue reached $2.85 billion in Q3, up 18% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter from Q2's $2.72 billion. This marks our ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit year-over-year growth, outpacing peers like Netflix's 8% and Disney's 11%. Breaking it down: subscription revenue, 68% of segment total or $1.94 billion, grew 22% year-over-year, fueled by a 12% increase in paid subscribers and 9% ARPU uplift from premium tier upselling. Advertising revenue surged 25% year-over-year to $720 million, or 25% of total, benefiting from ad-supported tiers and CTV inventory expansion, with AVOD and FAST channels seeing CPMs rise 15% to $28, comparable to Roku's mid-20s, thanks to better targeting via our AI-driven ad platform integrated with The Trade Desk. Content licensing and other contributed $190 million, up 8% year-over-year, including syndication deals for originals like the hit series Echo Frontier to international platforms such as BBC iPlayer.

Profitability stands out, with segment adjusted EBITDA hitting $920 million, a 28% year-over-year increase and a 32.3% margin—up 300 basis points from last year and ahead of Warner Bros. Discovery's ~25% in streaming ops. This reflects operating leverage from scale: content amortization costs as a percentage of revenue fell to 42% from 47%, aided by our fixed-cost library of 15,000+ hours. Free cash flow from the segment was $650 million, supporting $300 million in content capex this quarter, including greenlighting Season 3 of Quantum Edge and sports rights extensions.

On subscriber metrics, we ended Q3 with 28.2 million global paid subscribers across StreamGlobal's ad-light, ad-supported, and premium bundles—a net addition of 1.8 million in the quarter and 5.1 million year-over-year, for 22% growth. This outperforms Hulu's guidance and positions us in the top tier behind Netflix and Disney+.

Monthly churn improved to 3.2%, down 40 basis points year-over-year, thanks to our 'Watch Next' AI recommendation engine, boosting 90-day retention by 8% via personalized feeds leveraging data from 150 million MAUs. ARPU climbed to $12.85, up 7% year-over-year, driven by 15% uptake in our $17.99 Ultra tier with 4K/HDR, Dolby Atmos, and offline downloads, plus bundling synergies with telco wireless subs where 35% of new StreamGlobal adds came via zero-rated data plans on our 5G network, mirroring Verizon's +Play model.

Paid net adds by tier: Premium ad-free at 14.5 million ending with 0.9 million adds, up 18%; ad-supported 9.8 million with 0.7 million adds, up 28%; bundled telco 3.9 million with 0.2 million adds, up 15%; total 28.2 million with 1.8 million adds, 22% growth.

North America remains powerhouse at 72% of revenue, $2.05 billion up 16% year-over-year, with 20.1 million subs or 71% of total. Strength from live sports—GlobalSportsNet averaged 2.1 million primetime viewers, up 10%, bolstered by NBA and NFL carriage. FAST channel hours viewed spiked 40% to 1.2 billion, capturing share from Tubi and Pluto TV.

EMEA delivered $520 million, up 28% year-over-year, fastest-growing with 5.6 million subs via localized content like UK launch of Premier League Uncovered and French dubs of Echo Frontier; ARPU hit €11.20 or $12.10, premiumized by UEFA Champions League rights. APAC at $280 million, up 12%, faced India pricing caps but grew subs to 2.5 million through Jio and Singtel partnerships for bundled 5G streaming; investing $150 million in Hindi/Tamil originals to counter Hotstar.

For 2024 acceleration, three pillars: content pipeline with $4.2 billion annual spend, 25 new originals including a Game of Thrones-style epic with Amazon MGM Studios, renewed MLB and Premier League deals hedging linear decline down 5% to $450 million; tech initiatives like edge computing CDNs with Akamai reducing latency 35% for 5G live streams, HyperPersonalize ML increasing session length 22%, piloting password sharing crackdowns to unlock 1-2 million latent subs; monetization expanding hybrid AVOD+SVOD to 40% ad mix by FY24, telco bundling driving 25% of adds with LTV up 18% to $450 per sub.

We guide Q4 content and media revenue to $2.95-3.05 billion, up 17-20% year-over-year, EBITDA margins 32-33%, 1.5-2.0 million net adds.

Next, on new product and service launches' impact: In this hyper-competitive telecom and media landscape battling cord-cutters, OTT giants, and spectrum constraints, we've pivoted to bundled 5G Advanced and converged media using 3.5 GHz C-band spectrum from the 2021 FCC auction and edge computing.

In Q3, launches—primarily 5G Ultra Home FWA, StreamFusion bundle, AI-Powered Personalization Engine—drove $428 million incremental revenue, 12% of total quarterly wireless and broadband revenue of $3.6 billion, up 62% year-over-year from $264 million in Q3 2022, and 28% sequentially from Q2's $334 million post-5G SA core upgrade.

Subscriber-wise, 1.2 million net adds across postpaid mobile, broadband, converged—strongest since 2020 pandemic beta—bringing total base to 48.7 million, up 7% year-over-year. Postpaid phone 672,000 adds, broadband 412,000 mostly 5G FWA, StreamFusion video 156,000. Churn 0.9% for postpaid wireless below 1.1% target, sticky bundling lifting blended ARPU $4.72 to $58.43, 18% uptake of $85/month premium 5G Ultra tiers.

By product: 5G Ultra Home FWA targets suburban/rural with 300-500 Mbps at $60/month, competing T-Mobile/Verizon 5G Home, generated $212 million up 85% year-over-year from 289,000 net adds, 22% share in 15 priority DMAs per New Street; CAC fell to $320 from $450 via AI digital onboarding.

StreamFusion at $25 standalone or $15 add-on, 100+ live channels, 80,000 hours content including Peacock/Paramount+, low-latency HLS over 5G edge: $156 million revenue new launch, 156,000 subs, 45% penetration among new 5G Ultra, boosting video ARPU 32%, reducing churn 15 bps via AWS ML recs.

AI Personalization to 70% video footprint, federated learning drove 28% higher engagement, $60 million indirect revenue via premium upsells, 12% ad-supported growth.

Regionally: North America 85% new revenue, $364 million 1.05 million adds, Florida/Texas fiber-hybrid; Canada $28 million softer Rogers-Shaw overhang but 82,000 broadband; Europe 10% $43 million 112,000 adds UK/Germany StreamFusion with BBC; APAC 5% Australia trials $21 million 45,000 subs vs Telstra.

These underscore 'Converged Edge' integrating pipes with media to combat linear decline 8% per Nielsen, capture $150 billion FWA to 2027 per Dell'Oro; $1.2 billion capex 3.2x ROI on 5G Ultra, Warner Bros. Discovery content deal. Q4 guide $500-550 million new revenue, 1.4-1.6 million adds for 10-12% FY24 wireless growth.

Now, our revenue mix analysis: For Q3 and trailing trends, total revenue reflects resilience amid moderating demand, offset by digital media/enterprise growth.

Wireless services ~45% Q3 revenue, up from prior; driven 5G Ultra Wideband 95% North America coverage, 1.2 Gbps peaks matching Verizon mmWave with C-band; postpaid ARPU $52.47 up 2.1%, premium unlimited with Paramount+ 18% uptake; prepaid/IoT 1.2 million adds, enterprise IoT 15% from 5G private nets Ford/GM-like. U.S. 92%, Europe Vodafone JV 6% up 12% 5G SA, APAC India caps 2%; Open RAN Nokia/Samsung pilots cut capex 20%, $8 billion 2024 6GHz for 5 million FWA homes T-Mobile style.

Fixed broadband/wireline 28%, FTTP 15 million passings up 25%, gigabit 85% penetration vs AT&T 30 million; ARPU $68.22 up 4.3% multi-gig amid cord-cutting; voice down 8% offset business Ethernet 11%. U.S. 78%, Europe 9% UPC fiber Netherlands/Switzerland DOCSIS 4.0 10Gbps; $10 billion buildout Crown Castle urban, Akamai edge gaming/ARVR.

Media/entertainment 15%, up QoQ; DTC 45 million subs up 22%, GlobalCom+ $8.2 billion 92% DTC margins NFL Sunday Ticket-like; linear $7.1 billion steady 5% sub loss; licensing $4 billion up 18% Peacock/Hulu. North America 70%, EMEA 25% BBC co-prods, LATAM 8% telenovelas; AWS Bedrock AI 30% engagement churn 1.8%, M&A sports RSNs post-Diamond.

Enterprise solutions 9%, SD-WAN/cyber 16% Fortune 500 SASE Palo Alto; cloud Equinix 14%. U.S. 65%, APAC 20% Singapore/Japan, Europe 15%; $2 billion AI multi-cloud vs Cisco/VMware, $20 billion run-rate 2026 Industry 4.0.

Advertising/other 3%, CTV $2.1 billion up 25% 50 million smart TVs Trade Desk; DOOH; programmatic Google DV360 30% 2024 growth CCPA.

Mix shifts to wireless/media 61% from 56%, EBITDA margins +120 bps 42.3%; North America 82% +4%, EMEA 12% +10%, APAC/LATAM 6% +3%; $18.4 billion FCF $15 billion dividends/buybacks $5 billion M&A; 4-6% CAGR to 2026 integrated comms-media.

Finally, operating expense management: In Q3, $285 million year-over-year OpEx savings, trailing twelve-month $1.1 billion, OpEx/revenue down 12% to 56% from 68%, expanding EBITDA margin 320 bps to 44.2%, $2.4 billion EBITDA strongest Q2-like since 2021 merger.

Network ops/infra $142 million 50%: virtualization/Open RAN 28% hardware cut, 45% 4G LTE to cloud-native energy -22% vs 15% electricity spike AI data; Europe Nokia/Ericsson 15% TCO €65 million ~$72 million EU mandates; APAC Jio-like spectrum refarm $30 million defer capex 4.2 bits/Hz GSMA.

Content/programming $78 million 27%: reprioritize linear shed RSNs Diamond-like affiliate -18% $45 million; bundling 120 million mobile 12% down originals Warner; 30% user-gen short-form cost/hour $0.28 to $0.22 TikTok; LATAM $18 million AI dubbing ElevenLabs Brazil/Mexico FX.

SG&A/corporate $65 million 23%: AI customer care 65% Tier 1 Google Vertex from 42%, call center -25% $32 million NPS +8 churn 1.1% vs 1.4%; 10% non-frontline attrition upskill AT&T post-Warner 15 back-offices to 3 AI hubs $22 million real estate/travel; marketing data CAC -16% $45/sub Xfinity-like 5G pushes.

These fuel 3% ARPU $58.20, 6G prep; $285 million to bottom +$210 million EBITDA post-24% tax $0.42 EPS 15% beat. FY24 $1.2 billion savings 60% buybacks/FTTH vs 7.2 million cord-cut Moffett; risks FCC auctions strikes, diversified 55% telecom 45% media. U.S. opex 54% vs T-Mobile 52%, Europe 59% Ofcom, APAC 48%; margins high-end Big Four.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Sarah. I would like to provide an update on our network performance. We have made significant progress in expanding our 5G coverage to 95% in key markets, leveraging C-band and mid-band assets for Ultra Wideband speeds averaging over 1 Gbps. Our network reliability metrics continue to improve, with uptime exceeding 99.999% and latency reductions from edge CDNs supporting live streaming and IoT. We're seeing increased data usage across our customer base, up 25% year-over-year, driven by FWA trials and private networks. We are also actively working on enhancing our cybersecurity infrastructure, including SASE integrations and AI threat detection, to protect against rising risks in converged services. Our team's dedication to fiber convergence and Open RAN has been instrumental in achieving these results, enabling capex-efficient scaling and supporting our subscriber wins.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you discuss the competitive landscape and your strategy for maintaining subscriber momentum against fiber overbuilders and 5G FWA rivals?

Mark Thompson: Certainly, John. In this landscape with AT&T Fiber, Verizon Fios, T-Mobile 5G Home, and Starlink, our fiber-plus-5G convergence differentiates us—FTTH in 65% footprint, DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades, quad-play bundling at 62% new residential, best-in-class churn 1.1% residential 0.8% business. We're targeting 15-20% share in $200 billion market via $1.2 billion Q4 capex for 2.5 million FTTH passes, Northeast/Sun Belt wins like 15% MSA share vs Verizon, SMB Edge platform 28% trial conversion. Business outpaces with SD-WAN, private 5G logistics deals, ARPU $1,250. Full-year 400k-450k adds fund EBITDA growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for subscriber growth in the next quarter, and how will that impact content/media ARPU and margins?

Sarah Jenkins: We anticipate continued strength, with residential 220,000-250,000 net adds, total Q4 aligning FY 400k-450k. For content/media, Q4 $2.95-3.05 billion revenue 17-20% up, 32-33% margins, 1.5-2.0 million adds; new launches $500-550 million, 1.4-1.6 million adds boosting blended ARPU via Ultra tiers, bundling 35% zero-rated, ad CPM $28. OpEx savings $285 million/Q flow to 44.2% margins, AI personalization 7% ARPU lift to $12.85, LTV $450.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez: Can you provide an update on your fiber deployment plans and the expected ROI on those investments?

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Absolutely, Mike. Fiber passings expanding with $10 billion through 2025 to 15 million FTTP, 85% gigabit penetration, DOCSIS 4.0 symmetric 10Gbps Europe/U.S. via Crown Castle. Q4 $1.2 billion for 2.5 million new passes suburban underserved 40% cable vs 55% national. ROI strong—3.2x on 5G Ultra hybrid, CAC $320 broadband, business fiber lit 45% portfolio $1,250 ARPU 7% up. Open RAN cuts capex 20%, virtualization energy 22% savings support 6-8% broadband growth.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Mark, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Mark Thompson: Thank you. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy—from subscriber wins and media acceleration to opex discipline and network leadership—and deliver long-term value. Thank you for your time and interest in VeriStream Communications.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
